items.title: A ring map which becomes an isomorphism after inverting p is a universal homeomorphism exactly when its kernel is locally nilpotent and every element is bridged by a p-power multiple and a p-power
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter morphisms.tex (Morphisms of Schemes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a ring map which becomes an isomorphism after inverting a prime p, the induced morphism of spectra is a universal homeomorphism exactly when the kernel is locally nilpotent and every element of the target is bridged to the base by a p-power multiple and a p-power (statement lines 11825-11837). The counted proof is short but has real content: it uses an algebra criterion for the easy direction, reduces to an injective map by discarding the nilpotent kernel, forms the subalgebra of bridged elements, and then derives a contradiction from the two-step criterion for a proper subalgebra, in each of the two possible shapes, using that a p-power multiple of any element lands in the base because inverting p gives an isomorphism (proof lines 11839-11870). It is H2: both directions are carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being standard criteria for universal homeomorphisms and for subalgebras.
